gaps.sentence: If you ___ late again, the manager will have to speak to you.
gaps.hint: a warning about a real future
gaps.explanation: A real warning about the future keeps the if-clause in the present simple: are.

gaps.sentence: If the route ___ safer, I would cycle to work.
gaps.hint: an imaginary present situation, subjunctive were
gaps.explanation: Unreal present conditions formally take 'were' rather than 'is': were.

gaps.sentence: I will write down the address in case I ___ it.
gaps.explanation: 'In case' describes a precaution against a possibility and takes the present simple: forget.

gaps.sentence: If plants ___ enough light, their leaves turn yellow.
gaps.hint: a general truth in the if-clause
gaps.explanation: Zero conditionals state general truths with the present simple in both clauses: do not get.

gaps.sentence: Take some sun cream in case the weather ___ hot.
gaps.hint: in case plus present, a precaution
gaps.explanation: 'In case' is followed by the present simple even with future meaning: turns.

gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ you at the airport last week, but I was abroad.
gaps.hint: regret about a missed past meeting
gaps.explanation: Regret about something that did not happen takes 'wish' plus the past perfect: had met.

gaps.sentence: He wishes he ___ harder at school when he had the chance.
gaps.hint: past regret, wish plus past perfect
gaps.explanation: Regret about past behavior takes the past perfect after 'wish': had worked.

gaps.sentence: I wish the meeting ___ tomorrow; I would rather sleep in.
gaps.hint: a wish about a present arrangement
gaps.explanation: Wishes about present facts use 'were': were not.
